messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: help displaying all smoother in only one plot, hiding the raw data.
parts:
Hi Antonio, I don't fully understand the significance of the `tablename_x`, or why  they need to be connected with lines, so be cautious taking my advice.  Here is some code that may get you closer to what you want.  Be especially careful if the variability of the smoothed estimates is being correctly represented.  

When you say, "have all smoothers in only one plot",  I assume you mean "have all smoothers in only one facet/panel"?

ds <- subset(w1, ncase>10)
g <- ggplot(ds, aes(x=material_age, y=death.rate, color=B2))
g <- g + geom_smooth(aes(group=1))
g

Even if this is what you want, I'd still supplement it with a version of the faceted graph.  It can show the variability between years better than a single panel. Consider lightening up the lines using the alpha parameter in geom_line.  This series of graphs is probably getting complicated/serious enough that you need to use `ggplot` plus the geoms, instead of starting with `qplot`.

Consider if there's a way you can reintroduce the cells with low values of ncase, and then reestimate the variability.  But again, I don't understand the sampling structure of the dataset.
-Will Beasley

Thanks for your reply. Unfortunately, the code you kindly provided is not doing the job: instead it is producing different smoothers. To see this consider the plots for these different pieces of code:

# figure 1
qplot(data=subset(w1,ncase>10),y=death.rate,x=maternal_age,group=tablename_x,geom="line",ylim=c(0,.4))  +
opts(title="Under 2 deaths rates and Maternal Age by Survey whithin Years \n(minum number of cases by age-survey-year group is 10 children) ") +

geom_smooth(aes(group=1)) + facet_wrap(~B2)

# figure 2
qplot(data=subset(w1,ncase>10),
      y=death.rate, x=maternal_age, group=B2, colour=B2,
      geom="smooth",ylim=c(0,.4),se=FALSE) + 
  opts(title="Under 2 deaths rates and Maternal Age by Survey whithin Years: \nSmoothers")

# fugure 3
ggplot(subset(w1, ncase > 10),
       aes(y=death.rate, x=maternal_age, group=B2, color =B2) ) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  ylim(0, .4)

It might look a little better if you used alpha transparency on the
individual lines and maybe a somewhat thinner line width.

>
> In addition to this graph, I wonder if there is any easy to have all
> smoothers in only one plot, without displaying the raw data. I can send the
> data, if needed.

Of course :) Don't facet and use tablename_x as the grouping variable;
you probably want to use it as the color aesthetic, too. Given the
number of smooths involved, I'd suggest dispensing with the confidence
bands. Something like

qplot(data=subset(w1,ncase>10),
           y=death.rate, x=maternal_age, group=tablename_x, color = tablename_x,
           geom="smooth",ylim=c(0,.4))
or
ggplot(subset(w1, ncase > 10),
          aes(y=death.rate, x=maternal_age, group=tablename_x, color =
tablename_x) ) +
     geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
     ylim(0, 4)

I don't use qplot() very often so I don't know offhand how you'd set
se = FALSE inside the geom_smooth() call.

Dennis

parts:
I'm not 100% sure I understand exactly what you want, but I do think that the smoothers in 2 and 3 were the same as in 1. The only difference is that they're treated as a continuous variable for the purposes of the legend. If you want them to have the same color, you can do something like this:
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, group=factor(cyl))) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE)

And if you want them to have different discrete colors, you can do this:
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, colour=factor(cyl))) + geom_smooth(se=FALSE)

The factor(cyl) is so that a continuous variable, cyl, is treated as a discrete one for ggplot2.

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: help displaying all smoother in only one plot, hiding the raw data.
parts:
It just occurred to me that your data set is large enough that it might be switching from loess() (which is used for <=1000 points) to gam() for the smoothing model. What version of ggplot2 are you using? Recent versions (I think 0.9.2 and up) will print a message saying what kind of model is being used -- and they use a slightly different algorithm for determining which model to use.

You can do geom_smooth(method=loess) to force it to use loess in both cases.

-Winston
